input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi at home, so I rely on my phone for everything. Can you help me get my internet speed to be excellent?
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. What do you need me to do next?

At the top of my phone, I see a signal bar that looks pretty low, it says 2G, and there’s something about data being enabled. I also see something called “Data Saver.” Is that important? What should I do next?
Oh, I’m not sure which one to do first. Maybe let’s try changing the network mode to 4G or 5G? I really want the fastest speed possible. Can you help me with that?
Okay, I changed the setting like you said, and now at the top of my screen it says 5G and the signal looks excellent. But I still see that “Data Saver” thing. Should I turn that off next?
Alright, I turned off Data Saver, and now I don’t see it at the top anymore. What should I do next? Should I check my internet speed now?
I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. I thought everything was fixed since it shows 5G and the signal is excellent. Why would it still not work? What should I do now?
I’m not sure which one to do first. Maybe we can check the SIM card status? I don’t really know what APN means, so the SIM card sounds a little less confusing. Can you help me with that?
It says my SIM card is active and working. What should I do next?
I checked, and it says the APN name is “internet” and there’s an MMSC URL listed as “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look right, or do I need to change anything?

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t get any internet connection. The speed test still says “no connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working when everything looks fine at the top of my screen? What else can we try?
Oh, I definitely don’t want to change my plan—I just want to add more data for now. Can you help me add 2GB so I can get my internet working again? I really need it to be excellent, not just working.
I just ran a speed test, and it says my internet speed is excellent now! Thank you so much for your help—I really appreciate it. I feel much better knowing everything is working perfectly again.
Thank you so much for your help and patience with me. I really appreciate you walking me through everything step by step. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi at home, so I rely on my phone for everything. Can you help me get my internet speed to be excellent?

I can help you troubleshoot your mobile data issues and work towards improving your internet speed. First, I’ll need to identify your account to check your line and plan details. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you through the steps to resolve your mobile data issues.
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. What do you need me to do next?

Thank you for providing your information. To help improve your mobile data speed, I’ll need you to perform a few quick checks on your phone. This will help us identify what might be causing the slow or unreliable connection.

Are you able to check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any icons like Airplane Mode, signal strength bars, or network type (e.g., 5G, 4G)?
- If your phone shows “Data Enabled” or “Data Disabled”?

If you’re not sure how to check, let me know what you see at the top of your phone’s screen, and I’ll guide you through the next steps.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%

At the top of my phone, I see a signal bar that looks pretty low, it says 2G, and there’s something about data being enabled. I also see something called “Data Saver.” Is that important? What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. Here’s what I’ve found based on your description:

- Your phone is currently connected to a 2G network, which is much slower than 4G or 5G and will cause very slow internet speeds.
- “Data Saver” being enabled can also restrict your data speed and usage.

Let’s address these two issues step by step:

1. Change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, which will give you much faster speeds.
2. Turn off Data Saver mode to allow your phone to use data at full speed.

Would you like instructions on how to change your network mode first, or would you prefer to turn off Data Saver mode first? Let me know, and I’ll guide you through the process.
Oh, I’m not sure which one to do first. Maybe let’s try changing the network mode to 4G or 5G? I really want the fastest speed possible. Can you help me with that?

Great choice! To get the fastest speed, you should set your phone’s network mode to “4G/5G Preferred.” Here’s how you can do it:

1. Go to your phone’s Settings app.
2. Look for “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Find “Network Mode” or “Preferred Network Type.”
4. Select the option that says “4G/5G Preferred” or “LTE/5G.”

After you’ve changed the setting, please check the top of your screen again and let me know if you now see “4G” or “5G” instead of “2G.” If you’re not sure how to find this setting, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can give you more specific instructions.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%
Okay, I changed the setting like you said, and now at the top of my screen it says 5G and the signal looks excellent. But I still see that “Data Saver” thing. Should I turn that off next?

Yes, turning off “Data Saver” is the next step. Data Saver can restrict your phone’s ability to use data at full speed, which may still affect your internet performance even with a strong 5G signal.

Here’s how to turn off Data Saver:

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Look for “Data Saver.”
4. If Data Saver is ON, tap the switch to turn it OFF.

Once you’ve done this, try using your internet again and let me know if your speed has improved. If you’re still experiencing issues, we can run a speed test or check for any other possible causes.

Data Saver Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I turned off Data Saver, and now I don’t see it at the top anymore. What should I do next? Should I check my internet speed now?

Yes, that’s a great next step! Please try using your internet as you normally would, or you can run a speed test using your phone to see if your connection has improved.

If you notice any issues or if the speed is still not excellent, let me know what you experience (for example, if websites or apps are still slow to load). I can guide you through additional troubleshooting steps if needed. How is your internet speed now?
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. I thought everything was fixed since it shows 5G and the signal is excellent. Why would it still not work? What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your phone shows 5G with excellent signal but still reports “no connection,” there may be another issue affecting your mobile data. Common causes include SIM card issues or incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings.

Let’s try the following steps:

1. Check your SIM card status to make sure it’s active and properly inserted.
2. Check your APN settings to ensure they are correct.

Would you like instructions on how to check your SIM card status first, or would you prefer to check your APN settings? Let me know, and I’ll guide you through the process.
I’m not sure which one to do first. Maybe we can check the SIM card status? I don’t really know what APN means, so the SIM card sounds a little less confusing. Can you help me with that?

Absolutely! Let’s start by checking your SIM card status. Here’s how you can do it:

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap on “About Phone” or “About Device.”
3. Look for “SIM Status” or “SIM Card Status.”
4. Check if it says “Active,” “Ready,” “Missing,” or “Locked.”

Please let me know what your phone says about the SIM card status. If you see anything like “Missing” or “Locked,” let me know, and I’ll guide you on what to do next. If it says “Active” or “Ready,” we’ll move on to checking your APN settings.
Your SIM card is active and working.
It says my SIM card is active and working. What should I do next?

Great, your SIM card is active, so the next step is to check your APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to mobile data, even if you have a strong signal.

Here’s how you can check your APN settings:

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Select “Mobile Network.”
4. Tap on “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
5. Look for the APN name and check if there’s an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed.

Please let me know if you see an APN listed and if there’s an MMSC URL. If you’re unsure, you can tell me what you see on that screen, and I’ll help you determine if the settings are correct. If the APN or MMSC URL is missing or looks incorrect, I’ll guide you on how to reset your APN settings.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked, and it says the APN name is “internet” and there’s an MMSC URL listed as “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look right, or do I need to change anything?

Thank you for checking. Your APN name “internet” and the presence of an MMSC URL (“http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc”) both look correct for most carriers, so your APN settings appear to be set up properly.

Since your SIM card is active, you have a strong 5G signal, Data Saver is off, and your APN settings look correct, but you’re still seeing “no connection,” the next step is to try rebooting your device. Sometimes, a simple restart can refresh your network connection and resolve lingering issues.

Please restart your phone now. After it turns back on, try using your mobile data again and let me know if your internet connection is working. If it’s still not working, we’ll continue troubleshooting.

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t get any internet connection. The speed test still says “no connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working when everything looks fine at the top of my screen? What else can we try?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. Since you have a strong 5G signal, your SIM card is active, Data Saver is off, and your APN settings look correct, but you still have no internet connection, there may be an issue with your mobile line or account on our end.

I will now check your line’s status and data usage to see if there are any issues such as data limits being reached or a line suspension that could be affecting your service.
